title: Secure Outsourcing of Genotype Imputation for Privacy-aware Genomic Analysis (RO1HE21)
text:
:
Public Health Relevance. 
The personally identifying nature of the genomic data create risks of privacy breaches. We will develop and implement numerous computer-based methods that ensure genomic data is fully protected and the privacy of the participants are intact so that while an untrusted person, such as a genetic testing company, is analyzing data, they cannot directly gain access to an individual personal genetic information. The developed methods can improve public health by enabling the safe usage of the genetic information of patients while we analyze data, assess risks, and diagnose diseases using genetic data.

title: Identifying and understanding the mechanisms for increased risk of severe infection in obesity and diabetes
text: We have assembled a broad and highly accomplished team to continue our investigations of Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and infection, particular focusing on subjects that are vulnerable and seeking a deeper understanding of the effects of specific antibody glycosylation and specificity, bioinformatic signatures of pan virus responses and human immune organoids and the tissues and organs they interact with.

title: Automated Assessment of Infant Sleep/Wake States, Physical Activity, and Household Noise Using a Multimodal Wearable Device and Deep Learning Models
text:
A proliferation of wearable devices and machine learning approaches has led to exciting advances in automated
assessment of sleep, physical activity, and sedentary behavior in real-world environments. These methods,
however, have been predominantly developed and validated with adults and older children, and they do not
readily transfer to assessment of infant functioning in these key health domains. We aim to fill this gap by (a)
leveraging high-density multimodal data collected from a wearable device designed specifically for infants and
(b) developing deep learning algorithms to detect infant sleep/wake states, physical activity/sedentary behavior,
and household soundscapes.

title: A Chemical Footprinting Approach towards Poly-ADP-Ribosylation-regulated Biomolecular Condensation
text:
Aberrant protein Poly-ADP-ribosylation (PARylation) signaling is known to cause the misregulation of
biomolecular condensation and this underlies the pathogenesis of many neurodegenerative diseases, including
amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). However, the structural aspects of this
process are elusive. In this proposal, we will develop a chemical footprinting approach to characterize the
structural dynamics of PARylation-regulated phase-transition in the context of ALS and FTD.

title: Understanding the impacts of cancer therapy, high temperature and poor air quality on heart and lung health in breast cancer survivors.
text: Certain cancer therapies can lead to cardiovascular and respiratory problems among survivors, and prolonged high temperature and poor air quality increase survivors’ susceptibility to treatment-related health problems. We will determine whether survivors exposed to prolonged high temperature and poor air quality prior to diagnosis have a higher risk for therapy-related cardiovascular and respiratory problems, and if post-diagnosis short term exposure to extreme temperature and poor air quality during treatment increases survivors’ risk for cardiovascular and respiratory problems. The results will facilitate the development of behavioral interventions that oncologists and survivors can implement to mitigate treatment-related morbidity and mortality

title: Stem Cell/Organoid and Genome Editing Core
text: The overall goal of the Pluripotent Stem Cell and Organoid Core of the Digestive Health Center (DHC) is to provide DHC investigators with fully integrated services to catalyze research on mechanisms of digestive diseases via innovative and reliable model systems using native and genome edited stem cells and organoids. The Core pursues this goal with four complementary aims. In the First Aim “to provide DHC investigators with human iPSCs and iPSC-derived organoids and training,” the Core makes available to users quality-tested human pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) and PSC-derived multilineage cellular organoids of the esophagus, fundic and antral regions of the stomach, intestine, colon, and liver. The Core also facilitates the production of tissue- derived enteroids and liver and biliary organoids. These are novel 3D-miniature organs that enable studies related to physiology and pathobiology relevant to humans. Core leaders and experienced staff hold technology transfer through formal tiered courses and hands-on training, supervision, and support. In the Second Aim “to provide next generation organoid technologies for cheaper, scalable, high-quality organoids,” the Core provides investigators with the opportunity to generate organoids from healthy or diseased subjects using novel, reliable protocols for more efficient and scalable directed differentiation of human PSCs into organoids. In the Third Aim “to provide services for CRISPR-Cas9 mediated genome editing of human PSCs,” the Core evolved in its scope of technology and service to offer DHC Investigators state-of-the-art genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9 system. Successful projects have used knockin and knockout editing to study mechanisms of disease. To be able to track and visualize these cells in experimental assays, the Core also provide reporter-labeled PSC-editing and screening services to establish novel cell lines based on investigators’ needs. And in the Fourth Aim “to bank and make available quality-controlled iPSC lines and organoids for digestive research,” the Core banks well phenotyped natural and edited hPSC lines as well as disease-specific iPSCs to catalyze the translation of basic research findings into novel diagnostic and therapeutic tools. The service is aligned with high quality metrics and meets regulatory requirements for de- identification and human subject protection. Collectively, these novel technologies empower DHC investigators to study mechanisms of disease using multi-cellular experimental systems that have direct “lineage” to normal and diseased human tissues (including at different stages of maturation). The delivery of services is streamlined and centralized, and positions investigators to explore new collaborative projects to catalyze discoveries that will positively impact digestive disease research.

title: Elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the RBM15-MKL1 fusion protein in acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
text:
Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia is a pediatric cancer that lacks targeted treatment options and has variable
survival. The proposed research is relevant to public health because the elucidation of the molecular
mechanisms driving development of acute megakaryoblastic leukemia will provide avenues of investigation for
potential novel therapeutics and will enhance understanding of epitranscriptomic dysregulation in cancer. Thus,
the long-term goals of the proposed research will contribute to the part of the NIH’s mission that pertains to
advancement of scientific knowledge to understand illness and enhance health.

title: Multimodal characterization of affective visual processing in the early aftermath of trauma
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE/RELEVACE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) carries significant emotional, financial, and social burdens for affected
individuals and their families. Identification of neurobiological mechanisms that lead to PTSD development will
facilitate the generation of novel predictive models and preventative interventions. The results of the proposed
K01 are thus critical for the development of accurate neuroscience-based treatments for trauma and stress-
related disorders.

title: Aligning Machine Learning Models with Clinician Knowledge for Understanding, Prediction, and Prevention of Suicide
text:
The proposed research addresses fundamental data analysis challenges that have impeded efforts to predict,
prevent, and understand suicide in real-world contexts. It does this using a new paradigm to align deep learning
models with clinical knowledge. This project will yield (1) theoretically and empirically validated deep learning
methods especially designed for intensive longitudinal studies of suicide, (2) new insights/findings from existing
longitudinal data on suicide, increasing the scientific yield from previous NIH-funded projects, (3) a modeling
paradigm for embedding clinical knowledge in deep learning methods to improve forecasting performance, gen-
eralizable to other healthcare contexts, and (4) highly optimized, modular open-source code, available for the
broader community to apply and adapt to their needs.

title: Advanced high-content chemical imaging tools for phenotypic drug screening in 3D culture models
text:
Public Health Relevance/Narrative
Developing new drugs is a long and costly process, often taking over a decade and costing billions, with a high
rate of failure due to unexpected side effects and lack of effectiveness. Our project uses advanced imaging
technology coupled with innovations in machine learning to better predict drug efficacy and toxicity with advanced
cell culture models. By improving how we test drugs, this research could lead to accelerated drug discovery with
safer medications.

title: Targeting Amino Acid Metabolism in Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma ranks among the deadliest of all human cancers, with current therapies offering only palliation.
In this research project, we will study how amino acid metabolism stimulates glioblastoma cells to grow and
resist current therapies, empowering the design of potential new treatments for patients afflicted with
glioblastoma.

title: Mechanisms of Telomere-Mediated Lung Disease
text:
Telomere dysfunction is the most common identifiable cause of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The
connection with telomeres biology provides an opportunity to see IPF in a new way. This application seeks to
develop novel techniques and test hypotheses that connect telomere dysfunction and lung disease with an aim
of improving the lives of patients with telomere-mediated disease.

title: Role of Intraepithelial airway macrophages in lung homeostasis and disease
text:
Asthma is a common disease resulting from the pathologic activation of multiple cell types within the
conducting airways and is frequently driven by allergic inflammation to environmental antigens. Our preliminary
data suggests that airway lining cells can regulate immune responses by influencing the maturation state of
airway white blood cells through a signaling pathway called Notch. The proposed work uses advanced mouse
models of asthma, cutting-edge microscopy, and novel human culture methods to define the role of Notch
activation in airway white blood cells to reveal opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

title: Novel Lymphocyte Chemoattractant Receptor and Ligand
text:
Lymphocytes migrate from the blood into the various tissues of the body where they provide immunity to
infection and control cancer, but can also cause autoimmune and other inflammation associated diseases.
The focus of this application is on newly discovered mechanisms that control lymphocyte access to some of
the most clinically important organs in the body...including the lungs and airways, stomach, genitourinary tract
and the pancreas. The proposed studies could lead to improved vaccine strategies and to novel preventative,
therapeutic or curative treatment strategies for autoimmune, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases.

title: Molecular mechanisms that regulate ADAR target recognition and RNA editing
text:
The proposed studies in the parent grant seek to uncover fundamental rules for how the ADAR family of RNA
binding proteins recognize and chemically modify RNA in cells and how these events influence function and
health of neurons. The knowledge gained from our studies will contribute to understanding the over 35 human
diseases with altered ADAR function and the growing use of ADARs for therapeutic purposes. In this
supplemental proposal, I am requesting a Biorad ChemiDoc MP imaging system to undertake the proposed
experiments.

title: High-Resolution Supine Breast MRI
text:
While the mortality of breast cancer is signiﬁcantly decreased with screening mammography, magnetic res-
onance imaging (MRI) can potentially detect twice as many breast cancers, and is widely recommended for
women at increased risk of breast cancer, and with dense breasts. During breast MRI, the patient lies on her
stomach in a position that is very uncomfortable and limits the resolution, consistency across breast sizes, and
diagnostic sensitivity of imaging, as well as access for some patients. We propose to enable MRI with the patient
on her back with even sharper images that further improve diagnostic accuracy, in a position that is much more
comfortable and much more relevant to other procedures including ultrasound-guided biopsy and surgery.

title: PARP7 inhibition combined with radiotherapy to overcome ICI resistance in breast cancer
text:
Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) has had a transformative impact in triple negative breast cancer
(TNBC), yet there are still many breast cancer patients who have an incomplete response, and
alternatives to chemotherapy are needed to reduce long-term toxicity. The proposed study
investigates the use of PARP7 inhibition in combination with radiotherapy (RT) as a mechanism to
overcome ICI resistance and induce a systemic anti-tumor immune response in the absence of
systemic chemotherapy. If successful, this project will also provide a strategy to identify the breast
cancer patients who may be most likely to benefit from PARP7i/RT/ICI combination therapy.

title: Project 1: Combining PARP inhibition with radiation to sensitize HR proficient pancreatic cancers to immunotherapy
text:
(PROJECT 1)
Pancreatic cancer is the third leading cause of cancer-related death in the United States and is
associated with a grim 10% 5-year survival rate. The overall goal of this application is to develop
a therapeutic strategy using the combination of radiation with the FDA approved agent olaparib
to sensitize the majority of otherwise resistant pancreatic cancers to immunotherapy. The
preclinical and clinical studies in this proposal will lead to urgently needed advances in the clinical
management of locally advanced pancreatic cancer.

title: ORS Musculoskeletal Biology Workshop at Zermatt
text:
This Workshop is relevant to public health concerns because it brings a multi-disciplinary group of senior and
junior scientists together to discuss recent advances in musculoskeletal biology related to bone disease. The
Workshop will serve the junior scientist community and provide developmental activities and sessions, while
addressing pertinent questions and scientific advancement in our understanding of musculoskeletal disease. The
workshop provides vertically-oriented information, from basic science to clinical practice, to physicians,
scientists, and engineers who may not be completely familiar with all aspects of these diseases of public
health concern.

title: Cancer-related cognitive impairment: Real-time evaluation and assessment of long-term impact of treatment on young adult survivors (CRCI REALITY)
text:
Cancer and its treatment during adolescence or early young adulthood potentially disrupts normal frontal
neurodevelopment leading to cognitive dysfunction; however, sparse research on cognition in this vulnerable
population has relied primarily on self-report, with limited data on objective cognitive deficits. In this innovative
study, we propose to implement objective cognitive assessment in real-time in survivors’ daily life and measure
situational, behavioral, and contextual risk factors. By tailoring the assessment methodology to young adult
survivors, collecting pilot feasibility and acceptability data, then conducting a large, case-controlled study of
cognition in young adult survivors and matched non-cancer controls, we will provide much-needed data on the
prevalence of long-term cancer-related cognitive impairment and how to alleviate this problem in this vulnerable
population.
